statusVocabulary.supported: Source directly supports the bounded statement; physical visibility and route safety remain separate.
statusVocabulary.qualified: Usable with the stated qualification; source type or inference limits matter.

claims.claim: Queen's Ice Club in Bayswater opened in 1930.
claims.support: Museum interwar section and current venue history agree.
claims.limits: Use year; no need for opening-day, founder or oldest-rink claims.

claims.claim: London's indoor-rink expansion in the late 1920s and 1930s made skating a year-round participatory and spectator pastime instead of depending on frozen outdoor water.
claims.support: Article links interwar rink proliferation with year-round skating.
claims.limits: Context for Queens, not a claim it invented indoor or artificial ice.

claims.claim: The museum identifies a children's party at Queen's Ice Club. Direct image inspection shows children in summer clothing and skating boots, with an umbrella, wicker furniture and a boat with oars.
claims.support: Museum caption identifies event and venue; live browser image directly inspected at approximately 2026-09-21 15:21 UTC. See SOURCE-EDITORIAL-REVIEW.md.
claims.quote: Children's party held at Queen's Ice Club in Bayswater, London.
claims.limits: Exact date remains unconfirmed. Do not classify every costume as swimwear, infer a particular performance or music, or describe the mechanics of the staged scene.

verificationHistory.claim: The museum identifies a children's party at Queen's Ice Club; its image description shows children in swimsuits amid indoor beach props, including an umbrella and makeshift boat.
verificationHistory.support: Caption and descriptive image alternative; underlying image not independently visually inspected in this pass.
verificationHistory.limits: Undated here. Do not claim children skated in swimsuits or that the set stood on the rink's ice.
verificationHistory.outcome: Superseded after direct image inspection found the swimwear classification unreliable.

claims.claim: QUEENS remains an operating skating venue at 17 Queensway, with public sessions and lessons.
claims.support: Current activity and contact pages checked 21 September 2026.
claims.limits: No promise of a session being available without booking.

claims.claim: The official hours list Monday 10:00–23:00; the FAQ lists a £1 spectator/non-diner entrance charge.
claims.support: Dated operational check for evening planning.
claims.limits: Not essential narration. Keep stop exterior; do not direct a free interior visit.

claims.claim: William Whiteley began his drapery business in Westbourne Grove in 1863; it expanded to seventeen departments by 1867.
claims.support: Trust history provides chronology; archive locates the original shop and later row of premises.
claims.limits: Not the surviving Queensway building.

claims.claim: Whiteley marketed himself as a universal provider; the expanding business included house agency, decorating and food as well as clothing.
claims.support: Contemporary catalogue identity and custodian account of business expansion.
claims.limits: Slogan is not proof he could literally supply anything.

claims.claim: A surviving late-nineteenth-century Whiteley catalogue advertised toys and games alongside equipment for archery, croquet, lawn tennis, golf, polo and fishing.
claims.support: Object title, issuer and date range 1875–1900 identify these categories.
claims.quote: Archery, Croquet, La Crosse, Cricket, Golf, Polo, Fishing Tackle
claims.limits: Select a few categories in narration. No actual catalogue pages, prices or transaction observed.

claims.claim: The surviving department-store building dates from 1908–12, was designed by Belcher and Joass, and has a steel frame faced in Portland stone with giant classical orders.
claims.support: Statutory architectural description.
claims.quote: Steel framed with Portland stone facing.
claims.limits: Use accessible descriptions of visible columns; not Art Deco. No need to name architects unless explained.

claims.claim: The business moved from Westbourne Grove to the new Queen's Road store, now Queensway, in 1911.
claims.support: Archive's 15 November 1911 image record explicitly describes the move.
claims.limits: Do not transfer original shop scenes or 1907 death to this site.

claims.claim: Six Senses announced its London hotel open at The Whiteley in 2026; the wider redevelopment combines homes and commercial uses while retaining the listed frontage.
claims.support: Official opening announcement, not an earlier proposed-opening release.
claims.limits: No claim every shop is open, entry is unrestricted or regeneration benefits are proven.

claims.claim: The Trust's history says the business employed around 6,000 staff at its height and most lived in company dormitories.
claims.support: Custodian historical summary, credited to a 1992 history.
claims.limits: Reserve fact; do not locate all dormitories at the later Queensway store or invent individual workers' experience.

claims.claim: Whiteley's will left £1 million towards homes for older people of limited means, leading to Whiteley Village in Surrey.
claims.support: Institution's account of its founder and purpose.
claims.limits: Reserve; remote-site digression is probably unnecessary in this short stop.

claims.claim: During 1860s Underground construction, numbers 23 and 24 Leinster Gardens were demolished and a façade was erected to preserve the street's appearance.
claims.support: Henry Flather construction photograph, dated 1866–68, with museum description of the demolition and replacement façade.
claims.quote: a facade was erected to preserve the appearance of the street
claims.limits: Do not invent residents' demands, negotiations or a contemporary reaction.

claims.claim: Historic England lists the surviving terrace group and the screen wall equivalent to numbers 23 and 24; the group uses stucco and classical decorative forms.
claims.support: Listing names screen explicitly and describes terrace architecture.
claims.quote: screen wall forming equivalent of Nos 23 and 24
claims.limits: Listing's circa-1855 terrace date is not the screen's date. Visibility of fine details needs route check.

claims.claim: The early Underground used steam locomotives; the museum's 1866 Metropolitan Railway locomotive worked the Inner Circle until electrification in 1905.
claims.support: Museum-supplied vehicle history.
claims.limits: Do not generalise that all London Underground steam operations ended in 1905.

claims.claim: The open-air railway section behind the façades provided a place for steam-era trains to vent and for the underground route to obtain ventilation.
claims.support: Published route guide explicitly connects the false fronts with open-air venting; construction photograph independently supports the gap and screen.
claims.limits: Secondary technical explanation, not original engineering specification. Avoid claim that condensers remove coal smoke, exact wall thickness or every supposed design motive.

claims.claim: The council dates the start of fashionable residential development in the eastern Bayswater sector to 1827 and describes subsequent expansion westward during the nineteenth century.
claims.support: Historical Background, page 2; original sector bounded by Praed Street, Edgware Road and Bayswater Road.
claims.quote: development extended westwards as the century progressed
claims.limits: Not a date or single-master-planner claim for Queensborough Terrace or the whole route.

claims.claim: The council identifies large areas of nineteenth-century stuccoed residential terraces, classical architecture on a grand scale, and street patterns that give the neighbourhood visual unity.
claims.support: Key Features, page 2.
claims.limits: Area-level architectural context. Do not invent servant-floor arrangements or claim every façade is identical.

claims.claim: The council's 2004 guide describes many larger houses converted into flats within a still predominantly residential conservation area.
claims.support: Key Features, page 2, dated guide.
claims.limits: Historical area description, not proof of every building's current use. Hotel claims need separate observed or documented support.
